text:
The Matvei Michkov story in Philadelphia is about ice time, and it's loud. Rick Tocchet dismissed the idea that management forced him to play Michkov more, though PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor wrote that his version 'doesn't tell the whole story', especially across the first 11 games. Trade rumors followed, Sports Illustrated pitched him to the Islanders, and Bleacher Report ran a photo of a fan billboard calling for Tocchet's firing. Michkov is 21.

His minutes are rising, up 2.7 a night over his last ten to about 17.5. He has 10 goals in 21 games, but on only 5.5 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 34%. That will cool. Against it, the Flyers have scored 5.5 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, which has cost him assists and usually swings back.

He's already well ahead of most forwards drafted around him, at 0.71 points a game. Watch the minutes. If they keep climbing, the debate settles itself one way or the other.
headline: Michkov, the minutes and the noise
